messages.text:
The reference tree includes generated ptests, which is useful here: they tell me what the project itself considers observable CLI behavior.

I’m going to mine the option parsing and a sample of those tests, then I’ll implement the focused surface: listing, long view, tree, sorting, hidden handling, and no color/icon output.

commands.receipt:
> % eza(1) $version

<!-- This is the eza(1) man page, written in Markdown. -->
<!-- To generate the roff version, run `just man`, -->
<!-- and the man page will appear in the ‘target’ directory. -->


NAME
====

eza — a modern replacement for ls


SYNOPSIS
========

`eza [options] [files...]`

**eza** is a modern replacement for `ls`.
It uses [7mcolour[0ms for information by default, helping you distinguish between many types of files, such as whether you ar[0m
[7m[0me the owner, or in the owning group.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mIt also has extra features not present in the original `ls`, such as viewing the Git status for a directory, or recursi[0m
[7m[0mng into directories with a tree view.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mEXAMPLES[0m
[7m[0m========[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`eza`[0m
[7m[0m: Lists the contents of the current directory in a grid.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`eza --oneline --reverse --sort=size`[0m
[7m[0m: Displays a list of files with the largest at the top.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`eza --long --header --inode --git`[0m
[7m[0m: Displays a table of files with a header, showing each file’s metadata, inode, and Git status.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`eza --long --tree --level=3`[0m
[7m[0m: Displays a tree of files, three levels deep, as well as each file’s metadata.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mMETA OPTIONS[0m
[7m[0m===============[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--help`[0m
[7m[0m: Show list of command-line options.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-v`, `--version`[0m
[7m[0m: Show version of eza.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mDISPLAY OPTIONS[0m
[7m[0m===============[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-1`, `--oneline`[0m
[7m[0m: Display one entry per line.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--absolute=WHEN`[0m
[7m[0m: Display entries with their absolute path.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid settings are '`on`', '`follow`', and '`off`'.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to '`on`'.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m'`on`': Show absolute paths for all entries.[0m
[7m[0m'`follow`': Show absolute paths and resolve symbolic links to their targets.[0m
[7m[0m'`off`': Show relative paths (default behavior).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-F`, `--classify=WHEN`[0m
[7m[0m: Display file kind indicators next to file names.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid settings are ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’ (or ‘`auto`’ for short), and ‘`never`’.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to ‘`automatic`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`automatic` or `auto` will display file kind indicators only when the standard output is connected to a real terminal. [0m
[7m[0mIf `eza` is ran while in a `tty`, or the output of `eza` is either redirected to a file or piped into another program, [0m
[7m[0mfile kind indicators will not be used. Setting this option to ‘`always`’ causes `eza` to always display file kind indic[0m
[7m[0mators, while ‘`never`’ disables the use of file kind indicators.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-G`, `--grid`[0m
[7m[0m: Display entries as a grid (default).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-l`, `--long`[0m
[7m[0m: Display extended file metadata as a table.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-R`, `--recurse`[0m
[7m[0m: Recurse into directories.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-T`, `--tree`[0m
[7m[0m: Recurse into directories as a tree.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--follow-symlinks`[0m
[7m[0m: Drill down into symbolic links that point to directories.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-X`, `--dereference`[0m
[7m[0m: Dereference symbolic links when displaying information.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-x`, `--across`[0m
[7m[0m: Sort the grid across, rather than downwards.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--color=WHEN`, `--colour=WHEN`[0m
[7m[0m: When to use terminal colours (using ANSI escape code to colorize the output).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid settings are ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’ (or ‘`auto`’ for short), and ‘`never`’.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to ‘`automatic`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThe default behavior (‘`automatic`’ or ‘`auto`’) is to colorize the output only when the standard output is connected t[0m
[7m[0mo a real terminal. If the output of `eza` is redirected to a file or piped into another program, terminal colors will n[0m
[7m[0mot be used. Setting this option to ‘`always`’ causes `eza` to always output terminal color, while ‘`never`’ disables th[0m
[7m[0me use of terminal color.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mManually setting this option overrides `NO_COLOR` environment.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--color-scale`, `--colour-scale`[0m
[7m[0m: highlight levels of `field` distinctly.[0m
[7m[0mUse comma(,) separated list of all, age, size[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--color-scale-mode=MODE`, `--colour-scale-mode=MODE`[0m
[7m[0m: Use gradient or fixed colors in `--color-scale`.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid options are `fixed` or `gradient`.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to `gradient`.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--icons=WHEN`[0m
[7m[0m: Display icons next to file names.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid settings are ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’ (‘`auto`’ for short), and ‘`never`’.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to ‘`automatic`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`automatic` or `auto` will display icons only when the standard output is connected to a real terminal. If `eza` is ran[0m
[7m[0m while in a `tty`, or the output of `eza` is either redirected to a file or piped into another program, icons will not [0m
[7m[0mbe used. Setting this option to ‘`always`’ causes `eza` to always display icons, while ‘`never`’ disables the use of ic[0m
[7m[0mons.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-quotes`[0m
[7m[0m: Don't quote file names with spaces.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--hyperlink`[0m
[7m[0m: Display entries as hyperlinks[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-w`, `--width=COLS`[0m
[7m[0m: Set screen width in columns.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mFILTERING AND SORTING OPTIONS[0m
[7m[0m=============================[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-a`, `--all`[0m
[7m[0m: Show hidden and “dot” files.[0m
[7m[0mUse this twice to also show the ‘`.`’ and ‘`..`’ directories.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-A`, `--almost-all`[0m
[7m[0m: Equivalent to --all; included for compatibility with `ls -A`.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-d`, `--treat-dirs-as-files`[0m
[7m[0m: This flag, inherited from `ls`, changes how `eza` handles directory arguments.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: Instead of recursing into directories and listing their contents (the default behavior), it treats directories as reg[0m
[7m[0mular files and lists information about the directory entry itself.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: This is useful when you want to see metadata about the directory (e.g., permissions, size, modification time) rather [0m
[7m[0mthan its contents.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: For simply listing only directories and not files, consider using the `--only-dirs` (`-D`) option as an alternative.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-L`, `--level=DEPTH`[0m
[7m[0m: Limit the depth of recursion.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-r`, `--reverse`[0m
[7m[0m: Reverse the sort order.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-s`, `--sort=SORT_FIELD`[0m
[7m[0m: Which field to sort by.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid sort fields are ‘`name`’, ‘`Name`’, ‘`extension`’, ‘`Extension`’, ‘`size`’, ‘`modified`’, ‘`changed`’, ‘`accessed[0m
[7m[0m`’, ‘`created`’, ‘`inode`’, ‘`type`’, and ‘`none`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThe `modified` sort field has the aliases ‘`date`’, ‘`time`’, and ‘`newest`’, and its reverse order has the aliases ‘`a[0m
[7m[0mge`’ and ‘`oldest`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSort fields starting with a capital letter will sort uppercase before lowercase: ‘A’ then ‘B’ then ‘a’ then ‘b’. Fields[0m
[7m[0m starting with a lowercase letter will mix them: ‘A’ then ‘a’ then ‘B’ then ‘b’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-I`, `--ignore-glob=GLOBS`[0m
[7m[0m: Glob patterns, pipe-separated, of files to ignore.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--git-ignore` [if eza was built with git support][0m
[7m[0m: Do not list files that are ignored by Git.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--group-directories-first`[0m
[7m[0m: List directories before other files.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--group-directories-last`[0m
[7m[0m: List directories after other files.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-D`, `--only-dirs`[0m
[7m[0m: List only directories, not files.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-f`, `--only-files`[0m
[7m[0m: List only files, not directories.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--show-symlinks`[0m
[7m[0m: Explicitly show symbolic links (when used with `--only-files` | `--only-dirs`)[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-symlinks`[0m
[7m[0m: Do not show symbolic links[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mLONG VIEW OPTIONS[0m
[7m[0m=================[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThese options are available when running with `--long` (`-l`):[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-b`, `--binary`[0m
[7m[0m: List file sizes with binary prefixes.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-B`, `--bytes`[0m
[7m[0m: List file sizes in bytes, without any prefixes.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--changed`[0m
[7m[0m: Use the changed timestamp field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-g`, `--group`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s group.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--smart-group`[0m
[7m[0m: Only show group if it has a different name from owner[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-h`, `--header`[0m
[7m[0m: Add a header row to each column.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-H`, `--links`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s number of hard links.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-i`, `--inode`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s inode number.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-m`, `--modified`[0m
[7m[0m: Use the modified timestamp field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-M`, `--mounts`[0m
[7m[0m: Show mount details (Linux and Mac only)[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-n`, `--numeric`[0m
[7m[0m: List numeric user and group IDs.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-O`, `--flags`[0m
[7m[0m: List file flags on Mac and BSD systems and file attributes on Windows systems.  By default, Windows attributes are di[0m
[7m[0msplayed in a long form.  To display in attributes as single character set the environment variable `EZA_WINDOWS_ATTRIBU[0m
[7m[0mTES=short`.  On BSD systems see chflags(1) for a list of file flags and their meanings.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-S`, `--blocksize`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s size of allocated file system blocks.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-t`, `--time=WORD`[0m
[7m[0m: Which timestamp field to list.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: Valid timestamp fields are ‘`modified`’, ‘`changed`’, ‘`accessed`’, and ‘`created`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--time-style=STYLE`[0m
[7m[0m: How to format timestamps.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: Valid timestamp styles are ‘`default`’, ‘`iso`’, ‘`long-iso`’, ‘`full-iso`’, ‘`relative`’, or a custom style ‘`+<FORM[0m
[7m[0mAT>`’ (e.g., ‘`+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M`’ => ‘`2023-09-30 13:00`’).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`<FORMAT>` should be a chrono format string.  For details on the chrono format syntax, please read: https://docs.rs/chr[0m
[7m[0mono/latest/chrono/format/strftime/index.html .[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mAlternatively, `<FORMAT>` can be a two line string, the first line will be used for non-recent files and the second for[0m
[7m[0m recent files.  E.g., if `<FORMAT>` is "`%Y-%m-%d %H<newline>--%m-%d %H:%M`", non-recent files => "`2022-12-30 13`", re[0m
[7m[0mcent files => "`--09-30 13:34`".[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--total-size`[0m
[7m[0m: Show recursive directory size (unix only).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-u`, `--accessed`[0m
[7m[0m: Use the accessed timestamp field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-U`, `--created`[0m
[7m[0m: Use the created timestamp field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-permissions`[0m
[7m[0m: Suppress the permissions field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-o`, `--octal-permissions`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file's permissions in octal format.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-filesize`[0m
[7m[0m: Suppress the file size field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-user`[0m
[7m[0m: Suppress the user field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-time`[0m
[7m[0m: Suppress the time field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--stdin`[0m
[7m[0m: When you wish to pipe directories to eza/read from stdin. Separate one per line or define custom separation char in `[0m
[7m[0mEZA_STDIN_SEPARATOR` env variable.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-@`, `--extended`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s extended attributes and sizes.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-Z`, `--context`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file's security context.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--git`  [if eza was built with git support][0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s Git status, if tracked.[0m
[7m[0mThis adds a two-character column indicating the staged and unstaged statuses respectively. The status character can be [0m
[7m[0m‘`-`’ for not modified, ‘`M`’ for a modified file, ‘`N`’ for a new file, ‘`D`’ for deleted, ‘`R`’ for renamed, ‘`T`’ fo[0m
[7m[0mr type-change, ‘`I`’ for ignored, and ‘`U`’ for conflicted. Directories will be shown to have the status of their conte[0m
[7m[0mnts, which is how ‘deleted’ is possible if a directory contains a file that has a certain status, it will be shown to h[0m
[7m[0mave that status.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--git-repos` [if eza was built with git support][0m
[7m[0m: List each directory’s Git status, if tracked.[0m
[7m[0mSymbols shown are `|`= clean, `+`= dirty, and `~`= for unknown.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--git-repos-no-status` [if eza was built with git support][0m
[7m[0m: List if a directory is a Git repository, but not its status.[0m
[7m[0mAll Git repository directories will be shown as (themed) `-` without status indicated.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-git`[0m
[7m[0m: Don't show Git status (always overrides `--git`, `--git-repos`, `--git-repos-no-status`)[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mENVIRONMENT VARIABLES[0m
[7m[0m=====================[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mIf an environment variable prefixed with `EZA_` is not set, for backward compatibility, it will default to its counterp[0m
[7m[0mart starting with `EXA_`.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0meza responds to the following environment variables:[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `COLUMNS`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mOverrides the width of the terminal, in characters, however, `-w` takes precedence.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mFor example, ‘`COLUMNS=80 eza`’ will show a grid view with a maximum width of 80 characters.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThis option won’t do anything when eza’s output doesn’t wrap, such as when using the `--long` view.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_STRICT`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mEnables _strict mode_, which will make eza error when two command-line options are incompatible.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mUsually, options can override each other going right-to-left on the command line, so that eza can be given aliases: cre[0m
[7m[0mating an alias ‘`eza=eza --sort=ext`’ then running ‘`eza --sort=size`’ with that alias will run ‘`eza --sort=ext --sort[0m
[7m[0m=size`’, and the sorting specified by the user will override the sorting specified by the alias.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mIn strict mode, the two options will not co-operate, and eza will error.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThis option is intended for use with automated scripts and other situations where you want to be certain you’re typing [0m
[7m[0min the right command.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_GRID_ROWS`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mLimits the grid-details view (‘`eza --grid --long`’) so it’s only activated when at least the given number of rows of o[0m
[7m[0mutput would be generated.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mWith widescreen displays, it’s possible for the grid to look very wide and sparse, on just one or two lines with none o[0m
[7m[0mf the columns lining up.[0m
[7m[0mBy specifying a minimum number of rows, you can only use the view if it’s going to be worth using.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_ICON_SPACING`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the number of spaces to print between an icon (see the ‘`--icons`’ option) and its file name.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mDifferent terminals display icons differently, as they usually take up more than one character width on screen, so ther[0m
[7m[0me’s no “standard” number of spaces that eza can use to separate an icon from text. One space may place the icon too clo[0m
[7m[0mse to the text, and two spaces may place it too far away. So the choice is left up to the user to configure depending o[0m
[7m[0mn their terminal emulator.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `NO_COLOR`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mDisables colours in the output (regardless of its value). Can be overridden by `--color` option.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSee `https://no-color.org/` for details.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `LS_COLORS`, `EZA_COLORS`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the colour scheme used to highlight files based on their name and kind, as well as highlighting metadata and [0m
[7m[0mparts of the UI.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mFor more information on the format of these environment variables, see the [eza_colors.5.md](eza_colors.5.md) manual pa[0m
[7m[0mge.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_OVERRIDE_GIT`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mOverrides any `--git` or `--git-repos` argument[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_MIN_LUMINANCE`[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the minimum luminance to use when color-scale is active. It's value can be between -100 to 100.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_ICONS_AUTO`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mIf set, automates the same behavior as using `--icons` or `--icons=auto`. Useful for if you always want to have icons e[0m
[7m[0mnabled.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mAny explicit use of the `--icons=WHEN` flag overrides this behavior.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_STDIN_SEPARATOR`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the separator to use when file names are piped from stdin. Defaults to newline.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_CONFIG_DIR`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the directory where eza will look for its configuration and theme files. Defaults to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/eza` o[0m
[7m[0mr `$HOME/.config/eza` if `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is not set.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mEXIT STATUSES[0m
[7m[0m=============[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m0[0m
[7m[0m: If everything goes OK.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m1[0m
[7m[0m: If there was an I/O error during operation.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m3[0m
[7m[0m: If there was a problem with the command-line arguments.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m13[0m
[7m[0m: If permission is denied to access a path.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m

NAME
====

eza — a modern replacement for ls


SYNOPSIS
========

`eza [options] [files...]`

**eza** is a modern replacement for `ls`.
It uses [7mcolour[0ms for information by default, helping you distinguish between many types of files, such as whether you ar[0m
[7m[0me the owner, or in the owning group.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mIt also has extra features not present in the original `ls`, such as viewing the Git status for a directory, or recursi[0m
[7m[0mng into directories with a tree view.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mEXAMPLES[0m
[7m[0m========[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`eza`[0m
[7m[0m: Lists the contents of the current directory in a grid.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`eza --oneline --reverse --sort=size`[0m
[7m[0m: Displays a list of files with the largest at the top.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`eza --long --header --inode --git`[0m
[7m[0m: Displays a table of files with a header, showing each file’s metadata, inode, and Git status.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`eza --long --tree --level=3`[0m
[7m[0m: Displays a tree of files, three levels deep, as well as each file’s metadata.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mMETA OPTIONS[0m
[7m[0m===============[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--help`[0m
[7m[0m: Show list of command-line options.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-v`, `--version`[0m
[7m[0m: Show version of eza.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mDISPLAY OPTIONS[0m
[7m[0m===============[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-1`, `--oneline`[0m
[7m[0m: Display one entry per line.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--absolute=WHEN`[0m
[7m[0m: Display entries with their absolute path.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid settings are '`on`', '`follow`', and '`off`'.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to '`on`'.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m'`on`': Show absolute paths for all entries.[0m
[7m[0m'`follow`': Show absolute paths and resolve symbolic links to their targets.[0m
[7m[0m'`off`': Show relative paths (default behavior).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-F`, `--classify=WHEN`[0m
[7m[0m: Display file kind indicators next to file names.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid settings are ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’ (or ‘`auto`’ for short), and ‘`never`’.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to ‘`automatic`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`automatic` or `auto` will display file kind indicators only when the standard output is connected to a real terminal. [0m
[7m[0mIf `eza` is ran while in a `tty`, or the output of `eza` is either redirected to a file or piped into another program, [0m
[7m[0mfile kind indicators will not be used. Setting this option to ‘`always`’ causes `eza` to always display file kind indic[0m
[7m[0mators, while ‘`never`’ disables the use of file kind indicators.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-G`, `--grid`[0m
[7m[0m: Display entries as a grid (default).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-l`, `--long`[0m
[7m[0m: Display extended file metadata as a table.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-R`, `--recurse`[0m
[7m[0m: Recurse into directories.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-T`, `--tree`[0m
[7m[0m: Recurse into directories as a tree.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--follow-symlinks`[0m
[7m[0m: Drill down into symbolic links that point to directories.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-X`, `--dereference`[0m
[7m[0m: Dereference symbolic links when displaying information.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-x`, `--across`[0m
[7m[0m: Sort the grid across, rather than downwards.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--color=WHEN`, `--colour=WHEN`[0m
[7m[0m: When to use terminal colours (using ANSI escape code to colorize the output).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid settings are ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’ (or ‘`auto`’ for short), and ‘`never`’.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to ‘`automatic`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThe default behavior (‘`automatic`’ or ‘`auto`’) is to colorize the output only when the standard output is connected t[0m
[7m[0mo a real terminal. If the output of `eza` is redirected to a file or piped into another program, terminal colors will n[0m
[7m[0mot be used. Setting this option to ‘`always`’ causes `eza` to always output terminal color, while ‘`never`’ disables th[0m
[7m[0me use of terminal color.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mManually setting this option overrides `NO_COLOR` environment.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--color-scale`, `--colour-scale`[0m
[7m[0m: highlight levels of `field` distinctly.[0m
[7m[0mUse comma(,) separated list of all, age, size[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--color-scale-mode=MODE`, `--colour-scale-mode=MODE`[0m
[7m[0m: Use gradient or fixed colors in `--color-scale`.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid options are `fixed` or `gradient`.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to `gradient`.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--icons=WHEN`[0m
[7m[0m: Display icons next to file names.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid settings are ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’ (‘`auto`’ for short), and ‘`never`’.[0m
[7m[0mWhen used without a value, defaults to ‘`automatic`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`automatic` or `auto` will display icons only when the standard output is connected to a real terminal. If `eza` is ran[0m
[7m[0m while in a `tty`, or the output of `eza` is either redirected to a file or piped into another program, icons will not [0m
[7m[0mbe used. Setting this option to ‘`always`’ causes `eza` to always display icons, while ‘`never`’ disables the use of ic[0m
[7m[0mons.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-quotes`[0m
[7m[0m: Don't quote file names with spaces.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--hyperlink`[0m
[7m[0m: Display entries as hyperlinks[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-w`, `--width=COLS`[0m
[7m[0m: Set screen width in columns.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mFILTERING AND SORTING OPTIONS[0m
[7m[0m=============================[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-a`, `--all`[0m
[7m[0m: Show hidden and “dot” files.[0m
[7m[0mUse this twice to also show the ‘`.`’ and ‘`..`’ directories.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-A`, `--almost-all`[0m
[7m[0m: Equivalent to --all; included for compatibility with `ls -A`.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-d`, `--treat-dirs-as-files`[0m
[7m[0m: This flag, inherited from `ls`, changes how `eza` handles directory arguments.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: Instead of recursing into directories and listing their contents (the default behavior), it treats directories as reg[0m
[7m[0mular files and lists information about the directory entry itself.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: This is useful when you want to see metadata about the directory (e.g., permissions, size, modification time) rather [0m
[7m[0mthan its contents.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: For simply listing only directories and not files, consider using the `--only-dirs` (`-D`) option as an alternative.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-L`, `--level=DEPTH`[0m
[7m[0m: Limit the depth of recursion.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-r`, `--reverse`[0m
[7m[0m: Reverse the sort order.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-s`, `--sort=SORT_FIELD`[0m
[7m[0m: Which field to sort by.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mValid sort fields are ‘`name`’, ‘`Name`’, ‘`extension`’, ‘`Extension`’, ‘`size`’, ‘`modified`’, ‘`changed`’, ‘`accessed[0m
[7m[0m`’, ‘`created`’, ‘`inode`’, ‘`type`’, and ‘`none`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThe `modified` sort field has the aliases ‘`date`’, ‘`time`’, and ‘`newest`’, and its reverse order has the aliases ‘`a[0m
[7m[0mge`’ and ‘`oldest`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSort fields starting with a capital letter will sort uppercase before lowercase: ‘A’ then ‘B’ then ‘a’ then ‘b’. Fields[0m
[7m[0m starting with a lowercase letter will mix them: ‘A’ then ‘a’ then ‘B’ then ‘b’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-I`, `--ignore-glob=GLOBS`[0m
[7m[0m: Glob patterns, pipe-separated, of files to ignore.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--git-ignore` [if eza was built with git support][0m
[7m[0m: Do not list files that are ignored by Git.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--group-directories-first`[0m
[7m[0m: List directories before other files.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--group-directories-last`[0m
[7m[0m: List directories after other files.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-D`, `--only-dirs`[0m
[7m[0m: List only directories, not files.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-f`, `--only-files`[0m
[7m[0m: List only files, not directories.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--show-symlinks`[0m
[7m[0m: Explicitly show symbolic links (when used with `--only-files` | `--only-dirs`)[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-symlinks`[0m
[7m[0m: Do not show symbolic links[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mLONG VIEW OPTIONS[0m
[7m[0m=================[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThese options are available when running with `--long` (`-l`):[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-b`, `--binary`[0m
[7m[0m: List file sizes with binary prefixes.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-B`, `--bytes`[0m
[7m[0m: List file sizes in bytes, without any prefixes.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--changed`[0m
[7m[0m: Use the changed timestamp field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-g`, `--group`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s group.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--smart-group`[0m
[7m[0m: Only show group if it has a different name from owner[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-h`, `--header`[0m
[7m[0m: Add a header row to each column.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-H`, `--links`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s number of hard links.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-i`, `--inode`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s inode number.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-m`, `--modified`[0m
[7m[0m: Use the modified timestamp field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-M`, `--mounts`[0m
[7m[0m: Show mount details (Linux and Mac only)[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-n`, `--numeric`[0m
[7m[0m: List numeric user and group IDs.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-O`, `--flags`[0m
[7m[0m: List file flags on Mac and BSD systems and file attributes on Windows systems.  By default, Windows attributes are di[0m
[7m[0msplayed in a long form.  To display in attributes as single character set the environment variable `EZA_WINDOWS_ATTRIBU[0m
[7m[0mTES=short`.  On BSD systems see chflags(1) for a list of file flags and their meanings.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-S`, `--blocksize`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s size of allocated file system blocks.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-t`, `--time=WORD`[0m
[7m[0m: Which timestamp field to list.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: Valid timestamp fields are ‘`modified`’, ‘`changed`’, ‘`accessed`’, and ‘`created`’.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--time-style=STYLE`[0m
[7m[0m: How to format timestamps.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m: Valid timestamp styles are ‘`default`’, ‘`iso`’, ‘`long-iso`’, ‘`full-iso`’, ‘`relative`’, or a custom style ‘`+<FORM[0m
[7m[0mAT>`’ (e.g., ‘`+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M`’ => ‘`2023-09-30 13:00`’).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`<FORMAT>` should be a chrono format string.  For details on the chrono format syntax, please read: https://docs.rs/chr[0m
[7m[0mono/latest/chrono/format/strftime/index.html .[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mAlternatively, `<FORMAT>` can be a two line string, the first line will be used for non-recent files and the second for[0m
[7m[0m recent files.  E.g., if `<FORMAT>` is "`%Y-%m-%d %H<newline>--%m-%d %H:%M`", non-recent files => "`2022-12-30 13`", re[0m
[7m[0mcent files => "`--09-30 13:34`".[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--total-size`[0m
[7m[0m: Show recursive directory size (unix only).[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-u`, `--accessed`[0m
[7m[0m: Use the accessed timestamp field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-U`, `--created`[0m
[7m[0m: Use the created timestamp field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-permissions`[0m
[7m[0m: Suppress the permissions field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-o`, `--octal-permissions`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file's permissions in octal format.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-filesize`[0m
[7m[0m: Suppress the file size field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-user`[0m
[7m[0m: Suppress the user field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-time`[0m
[7m[0m: Suppress the time field.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--stdin`[0m
[7m[0m: When you wish to pipe directories to eza/read from stdin. Separate one per line or define custom separation char in `[0m
[7m[0mEZA_STDIN_SEPARATOR` env variable.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-@`, `--extended`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s extended attributes and sizes.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`-Z`, `--context`[0m
[7m[0m: List each file's security context.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--git`  [if eza was built with git support][0m
[7m[0m: List each file’s Git status, if tracked.[0m
[7m[0mThis adds a two-character column indicating the staged and unstaged statuses respectively. The status character can be [0m
[7m[0m‘`-`’ for not modified, ‘`M`’ for a modified file, ‘`N`’ for a new file, ‘`D`’ for deleted, ‘`R`’ for renamed, ‘`T`’ fo[0m
[7m[0mr type-change, ‘`I`’ for ignored, and ‘`U`’ for conflicted. Directories will be shown to have the status of their conte[0m
[7m[0mnts, which is how ‘deleted’ is possible if a directory contains a file that has a certain status, it will be shown to h[0m
[7m[0mave that status.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--git-repos` [if eza was built with git support][0m
[7m[0m: List each directory’s Git status, if tracked.[0m
[7m[0mSymbols shown are `|`= clean, `+`= dirty, and `~`= for unknown.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--git-repos-no-status` [if eza was built with git support][0m
[7m[0m: List if a directory is a Git repository, but not its status.[0m
[7m[0mAll Git repository directories will be shown as (themed) `-` without status indicated.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m`--no-git`[0m
[7m[0m: Don't show Git status (always overrides `--git`, `--git-repos`, `--git-repos-no-status`)[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mENVIRONMENT VARIABLES[0m
[7m[0m=====================[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mIf an environment variable prefixed with `EZA_` is not set, for backward compatibility, it will default to its counterp[0m
[7m[0mart starting with `EXA_`.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0meza responds to the following environment variables:[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `COLUMNS`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mOverrides the width of the terminal, in characters, however, `-w` takes precedence.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mFor example, ‘`COLUMNS=80 eza`’ will show a grid view with a maximum width of 80 characters.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThis option won’t do anything when eza’s output doesn’t wrap, such as when using the `--long` view.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_STRICT`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mEnables _strict mode_, which will make eza error when two command-line options are incompatible.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mUsually, options can override each other going right-to-left on the command line, so that eza can be given aliases: cre[0m
[7m[0mating an alias ‘`eza=eza --sort=ext`’ then running ‘`eza --sort=size`’ with that alias will run ‘`eza --sort=ext --sort[0m
[7m[0m=size`’, and the sorting specified by the user will override the sorting specified by the alias.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mIn strict mode, the two options will not co-operate, and eza will error.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mThis option is intended for use with automated scripts and other situations where you want to be certain you’re typing [0m
[7m[0min the right command.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_GRID_ROWS`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mLimits the grid-details view (‘`eza --grid --long`’) so it’s only activated when at least the given number of rows of o[0m
[7m[0mutput would be generated.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mWith widescreen displays, it’s possible for the grid to look very wide and sparse, on just one or two lines with none o[0m
[7m[0mf the columns lining up.[0m
[7m[0mBy specifying a minimum number of rows, you can only use the view if it’s going to be worth using.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_ICON_SPACING`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the number of spaces to print between an icon (see the ‘`--icons`’ option) and its file name.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mDifferent terminals display icons differently, as they usually take up more than one character width on screen, so ther[0m
[7m[0me’s no “standard” number of spaces that eza can use to separate an icon from text. One space may place the icon too clo[0m
[7m[0mse to the text, and two spaces may place it too far away. So the choice is left up to the user to configure depending o[0m
[7m[0mn their terminal emulator.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `NO_COLOR`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mDisables colours in the output (regardless of its value). Can be overridden by `--color` option.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSee `https://no-color.org/` for details.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `LS_COLORS`, `EZA_COLORS`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the colour scheme used to highlight files based on their name and kind, as well as highlighting metadata and [0m
[7m[0mparts of the UI.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mFor more information on the format of these environment variables, see the [eza_colors.5.md](eza_colors.5.md) manual pa[0m
[7m[0mge.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_OVERRIDE_GIT`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mOverrides any `--git` or `--git-repos` argument[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_MIN_LUMINANCE`[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the minimum luminance to use when color-scale is active. It's value can be between -100 to 100.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_ICONS_AUTO`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mIf set, automates the same behavior as using `--icons` or `--icons=auto`. Useful for if you always want to have icons e[0m
[7m[0mnabled.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mAny explicit use of the `--icons=WHEN` flag overrides this behavior.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_STDIN_SEPARATOR`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the separator to use when file names are piped from stdin. Defaults to newline.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m## `EZA_CONFIG_DIR`[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mSpecifies the directory where eza will look for its configuration and theme files. Defaults to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/eza` o[0m
[7m[0mr `$HOME/.config/eza` if `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is not set.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0mEXIT STATUSES[0m
[7m[0m=============[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m0[0m
[7m[0m: If everything goes OK.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m1[0m
[7m[0m: If there was an I/O error during operation.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m3[0m
[7m[0m: If there was a problem with the command-line arguments.[0m
[7m[0m
[7m[0m13[0m
[7m[0m: If permission is denied to access a path.[0m
